method: Multi-round parallel web search covering SEBI circulars and studies, academic VRP literature on SSRN/ScienceDirect/Journal of Futures Markets, CBOE benchmark research, NSE regulatory notifications, Oxford Business Law Blog, and GitHub repository topic searches; all claims linked to primary or secondary sources read during this session.

institutions.title: SEBI F&O Trader Study FY22–FY24 (September 2024): 93% of Individual Traders Lose Money
institutions.summary: SEBI studied over 1 crore individual traders and found that 93% incurred losses between FY22 and FY24, with aggregate losses exceeding ₹1.8 lakh crore (inclusive of transaction costs). The average loss was approximately ₹2 lakh per trader over three years; in FY24 alone, 7.3 million individual traders lost a net average of ₹1.2 lakh each. Only 7.2% of retail participants turned a profit over the period, and just 1% earned more than ₹1 lakh after costs. The top 3.5% of loss-makers averaged ₹28 lakh in losses each.
institutions.source_name: Business Standard / SEBI Analysis of Profits & Losses in Equity F&O FY22–FY24

institutions.title: SEBI F&O Study FY25 (July 2025): Individual Losses Widened 41% Year-on-Year to ₹1.06 Lakh Crore
institutions.summary: SEBI’s July 2025 update, covering 96 lakh unique traders across 13 major brokers, found individual net losses rose 41% to ₹1,05,603 crore in FY25 vs ₹74,812 crore in FY24 after transaction costs. Over 91% of traders still made losses, broadly unchanged from prior years. The number of unique individual F&O participants fell sharply from 61.4 lakh in Q1 FY25 to 42.7 lakh in Q4 FY25, partly due to SEBI’s lot-size and weekly-expiry reforms. A small reduction in aggregate losses was visible only in Q4 FY25.
institutions.source_name: Business Standard / SEBI FY25 Equity Derivatives Trader Loss Study

institutions.title: FPIs and Proprietary Traders Profit Overwhelmingly via Algorithmic Trading
institutions.summary: In FY24, FPIs booked gross trading profits of ₹28,000 crore and proprietary traders ₹33,000 crore from equity derivatives. SEBI found that 97% of FPI profits and 96% of proprietary-trader profits came from algorithmic trading entities; by FY26 this rose to 99% for both categories. Proprietary desks earned ₹44,483 crore in FY26 (down only 3%), while FPI profits fell 55% to ₹13,896 crore following the Jane Street disruption. Only 13% of retail traders used any algorithm, and even that figure is overstated because it includes broker-forced intraday liquidation systems.
institutions.source_name: Zerodha TradingQnA / SEBI FY22–FY24 Algo vs Non-Algo Profit Breakdown

institutions.title: SEBI Interim Order Against Jane Street (July 2025): Alleged Two-Phase Index Manipulation on 18 Expiry Days
institutions.summary: On 3 July 2025, SEBI issued a 105-page interim order barring Jane Street (JSI Investments, Jane Street Singapore, Jane Street Asia Trading) from Indian markets and seizing ₹4,840 crore (~$570 million) in alleged ill-gotten gains. SEBI alleged that across 18 derivative expiry days from January 2023 to March 2025, Jane Street ran a two-phase pattern: in Patch I (9:15–11:46 AM) it aggressively bought Bank Nifty component stocks (often >20% of market-wide traded value in Kotak Bank, SBI, Axis Bank) pushing the index up, then in Patch II reversed positions to drive the index down at expiry, benefiting its large short-options book. Jane Street’s India arm recorded net profits of ~₹36,500 crore over January 2023–March 2025; the firm deposited ₹4,843.5 crore into SEBI’s escrow by 14 July 2025 and is contesting the findings in litigation.
institutions.source_name: Oxford Business Law Blog / Jane Street and the Expiry Day Trap: Unpacking SEBI’s Crackdown on Algorithmic Manipulation in India

institutions.title: SEBI Index Derivatives Reform Package (October–November 2024): Six Measures to Curb Retail Speculation
institutions.summary: SEBI circular SEBI/HO/MRD/TPD-1/P/CIR/2024/132 (1 October 2024) introduced six measures effective 20 November 2024: (1) one weekly expiry per exchange—Nifty 50 on NSE, Sensex on BSE; Bank Nifty, Nifty Financial Services, Nifty Midcap Select, Sensex 50, and BANKEX weekly expiries all discontinued; (2) minimum contract size raised to ₹15 lakh (Nifty lot size 25→75 units); (3) Extreme Loss Margin of 2% on short positions on expiry day; (4) intraday position monitoring at least four times daily; (5) removal of calendar-spread margin treatment on expiry day; (6) upfront collection of full options premiums from buyers, effective 1 February 2025.
institutions.source_name: Zerodha Z-Connect / SEBI October 2024 F&O Index Derivatives Rules

institutions.title: Nifty Weekly Expiry Moved Thursday→Tuesday (September 2025) and Delta-Based OI Limits Introduced
institutions.summary: Effective 1 September 2025, NSE moved all Nifty contract expiries from Thursday to Tuesday (first expiry 2 September 2025); simultaneously BSE moved Sensex expiries to Thursday, completing a regulatory swap so the two major indices no longer expire on the same day. Separately, SEBI replaced binary open-interest counting with delta-based OI (DeltaOI): each options position is weighted by its delta rather than counting every contract equally, so deep-ITM options contribute more to the OI limit than far-OTM options, more accurately reflecting true market exposure and determining F&O stock ban lists.
institutions.source_name: Zerodha MarketIntel / NSE F&O Contract Expiry Day Revision September 2025

institutions.title: Global HFT and Market-Making Firms Scaling India Operations (2024–2026)
institutions.summary: India generated nearly 60% of global equity derivatives volumes in April 2025, drawing aggressive expansion from US and European firms. Citadel Securities India revenues grew 39% to $450 million in the most recent year—a sixfold increase since the unit launched ~3 years earlier. IMC Trading planned to expand its India team by >50% to 150+ staff by end-2026. Optiver opened a Mumbai office in 2024 targeting 100 India-based employees. Millennium Management is scaling its India desk from Dubai and Singapore. NSE committed to adding 2,000 co-location racks over two years to meet microsecond-execution demand. Citadel, IMC, Optiver, and others are also on SEBI’s heightened surveillance radar following the Jane Street action.
institutions.source_name: HedgeWeek / Global Derivatives Traders Boost India Presence (2025)

institutions.title: NSE Algorithmic Trading: 70% of F&O Turnover; HFT Firms Capture Virtually All Institutional Profits
institutions.summary: Algorithmic trading accounts for approximately 70% of all Futures and Options trades on the NSE by turnover, with HFT firms executing thousands of orders per second using NSE co-location facilities. The SEBI FY22–FY24 study confirmed that this infrastructure advantage is the primary mechanism by which FPIs and prop desks systematically capture profits from retail order flow. Options premiums on NSE surged 11-fold in the five years to March 2025, and NSE’s index options segment holds over 90% domestic market share, making it the world’s largest equity index options exchange by contract count during peak periods.
institutions.source_name: Wright Research / SEBI F&O Report: Who Profits in Indian Index Options

strategies.name: Short Strangle (Volatility Risk Premium Harvesting)
strategies.who_uses: Proprietary trading desks, hedge funds (systematic vol sellers), HFT market makers
strategies.legs: Sell OTM call + sell OTM put, same expiry; typically 15–30 delta on each side. Net credit received.
strategies.edge_source: Implied volatility consistently exceeds realized volatility in equity index options (the variance risk premium). Sellers collect the spread between expensive implied vol and cheaper realized vol over time. Documented to be profitable on Nifty options (Garg & Vipul 2015; SSRN 2026 study).
strategies.main_risk: Unlimited loss if the index makes a large directional move beyond either short strike; gap or black-swan events can produce catastrophic losses.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — naked short positions require very high margin, constant monitoring, and strict stop-loss discipline; a single large move can exceed entire capital

strategies.name: Iron Condor (Defined-Risk Short Strangle)
strategies.who_uses: Retail and semi-professional options traders, structured product desks, systematic income strategies
strategies.legs: Sell OTM call + buy further OTM call (call credit spread) + sell OTM put + buy further OTM put (put credit spread); all same expiry. Net credit, capped maximum loss.
strategies.edge_source: Harvests the volatility risk premium with defined risk. Bought wings cap the maximum loss, making the trade capital-efficient relative to a naked strangle while still exploiting IV > RV. Loss is always bounded by the width of the widest spread minus credit received.
strategies.main_risk: Loss if underlying breaches either short strike at expiry; maximum loss is width of spread minus credit received.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — defined risk is clear upfront; manageable for disciplined traders with a basic options platform

strategies.name: Covered Call / Index Overwriting
strategies.who_uses: Mutual funds, insurance portfolios, DII asset managers, large institutional equity holders generating yield
strategies.legs: Long underlying index ETF or equivalent basket + short OTM call at the same or next expiry. Rolled at each monthly or weekly expiry.
strategies.edge_source: The CBOE BXM covered-call benchmark earned 8.5% annualized (1986–2026) with substantially lower volatility than the S&P 500. Equity holders enhance income in flat or declining markets by monetizing the volatility risk premium embedded in call options.
strategies.main_risk: Upside capped if the index rallies beyond the short call strike; full downside exposure on the underlying long position remains.
strategies.retail_suitability: high — straightforward for anyone who owns the underlying ETF; the risk is opportunity cost, not additional capital loss

strategies.name: Cash-Secured Put Write (PUT Index Strategy)
strategies.who_uses: Asset managers, family offices, systematic income strategies, institutional pension overlays
strategies.legs: Sell ATM or slightly OTM put each monthly (or weekly) expiry; hold cash equal to strike × lot size as collateral. Roll at expiry.
strategies.edge_source: The CBOE PUT index outperformed the S&P 500 on a risk-adjusted basis with a Sharpe ratio 46% higher over 32+ years (Bondarenko 2019). Structural demand for put protection from portfolio hedgers inflates put implied vol above fair value, creating a persistent premium for systematic sellers.
strategies.main_risk: Assignment (economic) loss if index falls sharply below the strike; economic loss equals (strike − spot) × lot size minus premium received.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — large cash requirement per lot (₹15L+ post-2024 reform), but risk is identical to holding the index; suitable for income-oriented traders with adequate capital

strategies.name: Protective Put / Portfolio Insurance
strategies.who_uses: Institutional equity funds, mutual funds, large portfolio managers hedging drawdown risk ahead of macro events
strategies.view: bullish on index, hedging tail risk
strategies.legs: Long underlying index basket + long OTM put (5–10% OTM) at monthly or quarterly expiry.
strategies.edge_source: Provides asymmetric protection against large drawdowns while retaining full upside participation. Portfolio insurance demand from institutional holders is precisely what inflates put implied vol above fair value, creating the VRP that sellers harvest on the other side.
strategies.main_risk: Ongoing premium cost erodes returns in steadily rising markets; the volatility drag can be substantial in low-vol or trending regimes.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — straightforward concept; suitable as a hedge if holding large index exposure, but recurring premium costs require budgeting

strategies.name: Collar (Zero-Cost Hedge: Protective Put + Covered Call)
strategies.who_uses: Institutional equity holders, corporate treasuries hedging concentrated positions, conservative HNI retail
strategies.legs: Long underlying + long OTM put (lower strike) + short OTM call (higher strike), same expiry. Call premium partially or fully finances the put, creating a zero-cost or low-cost hedge.
strategies.edge_source: A zero-cost collar eliminates downside beyond the put strike at near-zero net premium by financing the put with call sales. Widely used by institutions to monetize large equity positions without selling and triggering capital-gains tax.
strategies.main_risk: Upside is capped by the short call strike; complex tax treatment in some jurisdictions for equity-based collars.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — requires holding the underlying and managing two option legs; the logic is intuitive for most equity investors

strategies.name: Bear Put Spread (Put Spread Hedge)
strategies.who_uses: Equity funds, risk managers, directional retail traders expecting moderate decline
strategies.legs: Buy ATM or slightly OTM put + sell lower-strike OTM put, same expiry. Net debit. Maximum profit is the spread width minus net premium paid.
strategies.edge_source: Reduces the cost of put protection relative to outright puts by selling a lower put. Exploits the volatility skew (lower-strike puts command higher IV due to structural demand) to reduce the premium paid for the hedge. Defined-risk trade with clear maximum profit and loss at inception.
strategies.main_risk: Maximum profit is capped between strikes; no protection below the lower short put strike. Full debit is lost if the index stays above the long put strike.
strategies.retail_suitability: high — limited cost, fully defined risk, simple to understand; the most accessible directional hedge for retail traders

strategies.name: Calendar Spread (Time Spread / Horizontal Spread)
strategies.who_uses: Volatility desks, professional options traders, prop desks exploiting term-structure mispricing
strategies.legs: Sell near-term ATM option + buy same-strike further-term option. Net debit. Profits if near-term vol stays elevated, or if spot stays near the strike through the near-term expiry.
strategies.edge_source: Exploits term-structure mispricing or the faster theta decay of near-term options vs long-term options. Near-term options embed higher annualized IV than longer-term options around scheduled events, creating a roll-down opportunity for the short leg.
strategies.main_risk: Vega risk: if long-dated IV collapses, the long leg loses value. Large spot moves away from strike make both legs OTM and unprofitable simultaneously.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires understanding of two expiry cycles, term structure, and active management; complex SPAN margin treatment in India

strategies.name: Diagonal Spread (Poor Man’s Covered Call / Calendar + Vertical)
strategies.who_uses: Retail options traders with directional views, smaller prop desks managing longer-term delta exposure
strategies.view: mildly bullish (call diagonal) or mildly bearish (put diagonal)
strategies.legs: Buy longer-dated ITM/ATM option + sell shorter-dated OTM option at a different strike and expiry. Roll the short leg each expiry to generate ongoing income against the long anchor leg.
strategies.edge_source: Provides long-delta exposure at lower capital than buying the underlying, while collecting theta from the short near-term leg. The long leg retains substantial time value, reducing cost relative to a covered call on the underlying.
strategies.main_risk: Long vega on the back leg: both legs can lose value if volatility collapses. Maximum loss is limited to the net debit paid.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — limited risk but requires tracking two expiries; more capital-efficient than covered calls without owning the underlying

strategies.name: Dispersion Trade (Correlation Risk Premium)
strategies.who_uses: Banks (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup vol desks), volatility arbitrage hedge funds; assets in dispersion strategies at least doubled 2021–2024
strategies.view: volatility arbitrage — short correlation, long single-stock vol
strategies.legs: Short index variance swap (or ATM straddle on index) + long variance swaps (or straddles) on a basket of index constituents, weighted by index composition. Position sized so notional variance exposures are delta-neutral.
strategies.edge_source: Index implied vol systematically exceeds the weighted-average constituent implied vol because portfolio hedgers bid up index options more than single-stock options. Banks monetize the gap between implied correlation (in expensive index options) and realized correlation (actual co-movement). This correlation risk premium is structural and persistent.
strategies.main_risk: Correlation spike during risk-off events: when stocks fall together, index vol can exceed constituent vols, generating losses on both legs simultaneously. Large notional positions require significant capital.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires access to variance swaps or precise multi-leg straddle management across 50 stocks simultaneously; institutionally scaled capital and infrastructure required

strategies.name: Gamma Scalping (Dynamic Delta Hedging of Long Options)
strategies.who_uses: Market makers, volatility desks, hedge funds running long-gamma books; documented as the primary mechanism for extracting VRP on the long side
strategies.view: volatility — profitable when realized volatility exceeds implied volatility paid
strategies.legs: Long ATM straddle (or other long-gamma position) + continuously delta-hedge by buying/selling the underlying Nifty futures to remain delta-neutral after each spot move.
strategies.edge_source: P&L ≈ ½ × gamma × (RV² − IV²) × time. Each delta-hedge trade locks in a small P&L proportional to gamma times (spot move squared). Profitable if realized vol exceeds the implied vol embedded in the options premium paid.
strategies.main_risk: Theta cost: long options decay daily; if realized vol is insufficient the position bleeds theta. Transaction costs of continuous hedging (SPAN margins, bid-ask on futures) consume gross gamma P&L.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires real-time delta monitoring, fast execution infrastructure (co-location or DMA), and deep understanding of the gamma-theta trade-off; not feasible with EOD data alone

strategies.name: Volatility Skew Trade (Put-Call Skew Arb)
strategies.who_uses: Hedge funds, volatility desks, sophisticated proprietary traders monitoring the implied vol surface
strategies.legs: Sell relatively expensive OTM put + buy relatively cheap OTM call at the same delta (e.g., 25-delta risk reversal); or vice versa if call skew is elevated. Sized to be dollar-delta neutral.
strategies.edge_source: Index put skew (put IV > call IV at equal delta) typically exceeds its historically realized level due to structural demand for downside puts. Selling the expensive side and buying the cheap side captures the mean-reversion of implied skew toward realized skew. Skew risk premium documented in global index options research.
strategies.main_risk: Skew can widen further before mean-reverting; positions are sensitive to changes in both spot level and overall vol, not just the IV spread between puts and calls.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires detailed understanding of the options surface, live IV data at multiple strikes, and delta management; not accessible with basic platforms

strategies.name: Expiry-Day Theta Selling (0-DTE or Near-Zero-DTE Short Options)
strategies.who_uses: Indian retail traders and HNI desk traders (very popular pre-2024 SEBI reform); small proprietary desks; algo sellers
strategies.legs: Sell ATM straddle or OTM strangle on morning of weekly expiry (now Tuesdays on NSE from September 2025); aim to close before market close as extrinsic value collapses to near zero.
strategies.edge_source: On expiry day all remaining extrinsic value decays to zero within hours. A larger implied move is typically priced into the open-of-day premium than the index actually realizes during the session, on average. NSE’s weekly expiry structure provided multiple opportunities per month before 2024 reforms reduced available indices.
strategies.main_risk: Sudden large intraday moves from news or alleged manipulative price action (as per SEBI’s Jane Street order) can cause catastrophic losses; theoretically unlimited without hedging wings. Post November 2024, SEBI’s ELM of 2% on short positions on expiry day increased margin requirements.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires constant intraday monitoring; SEBI’s 2024 ELM margin increase made this less capital-efficient; small moves against position can rapidly exceed premium collected

strategies.name: Delta-Hedged Market Making (Options Market Making)
strategies.who_uses: HFT/market-making firms: Jane Street, Citadel Securities, Optiver, IMC Trading; NSE co-location participants; the dominant mode of institutional engagement in Indian index options
strategies.legs: Quote bids and offers in multiple option strikes and expiries across the Nifty option chain; instantly delta-hedge every fill using Nifty futures or the underlying basket; collect bid-ask spread on every trade. Maintain flat or near-flat net delta book, with positive gamma/vega exposure.
strategies.edge_source: Structural edge from bid-ask spread captured on every fill, supplemented by superior execution speed via co-location, proprietary IV and risk models, and risk aggregation across thousands of simultaneous quotes. SEBI data shows 99% of FPI and prop-trader profits in FY26 came from algo entities using this approach.
strategies.main_risk: Adverse selection (being systematically hit by better-informed flow); inventory risk during fast markets; regulatory scrutiny from SEBI’s heightened surveillance (Jane Street SEBI order July 2025).
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires co-location, sub-millisecond execution, capital >10 crore, and sophisticated real-time risk systems; completely inaccessible to retail

strategies.name: Long Straddle (Volatility Buying / Event-Driven Options)
strategies.who_uses: Event-driven hedge funds, macro traders around RBI policy/Union Budget/global shocks, retail traders expecting large moves
strategies.view: volatility — profits from a large move in either direction
strategies.legs: Buy ATM call + buy ATM put, same strike and expiry. Net debit. Maximum loss is total premium paid; unlimited profit potential in either direction.
strategies.edge_source: Profitable when realized volatility exceeds the implied volatility priced into the options. Most effective before scheduled macro events (RBI policy meetings, Union Budget, global shock) when the actual index move is likely to be large relative to the premium paid.
strategies.main_risk: Theta decay: both legs lose value every day the index stays near the strike. In the majority of non-event periods IV > RV, making buyers the losing side on average (the VRP works against long-straddle buyers).
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — loss is limited to premium paid; no margin beyond SPAN required; intuitive concept, but the trader is fighting the volatility risk premium in non-event periods

strategies.name: Butterfly Spread (Sell-the-Middle Low-Cost Neutral Trade)
strategies.who_uses: Retail and semi-professional traders targeting very low-volatility environments; structured product desks
strategies.view: neutral — maximum profit if spot expires exactly at the middle strike
strategies.legs: Buy 1 ITM option + sell 2 ATM options + buy 1 OTM option, all same expiry and equidistant strikes. Net small debit (call butterfly) or credit (put butterfly).
strategies.edge_source: Cheap, defined-risk position that pays off if the index settles exactly at the middle strike at expiry. Useful when implied vol is high (premium collected at center) but the trader expects the market to stay in a tight range. Maximum profit = width of wings minus net debit.
strategies.main_risk: Narrow profit zone; maximum profit only if spot pins the middle strike at expiry. Maximum loss equals net debit paid.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — limited, defined risk; suitable for retail targeting a specific price level; requires precise strike selection and understanding of the payoff profile

strategies.name: Ratio Spread (1×2 Call or Put Ratio)
strategies.who_uses: Professional traders, prop desks, vol sellers who want enhanced premium versus a simple spread
strategies.view: mildly directional: call ratio = mildly bullish, but profits from flat/slight rally; put ratio = mildly bearish
strategies.legs: Buy 1 ATM or near-ATM option + sell 2 OTM options (same type, same expiry). Small net credit or near-zero net premium.
strategies.edge_source: Collects more premium than a simple spread by selling an extra OTM option. Profits from time decay as long as the index doesn’t move strongly in the direction of the short options. Profitable across a range of outcomes beyond the breakeven point.
strategies.main_risk: Uncapped loss beyond the double-short strike (for call ratio spread, unlimited losses in a strong rally). Can produce large losses in sharp directional moves or gap events.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — uncapped risk on one side requires robust risk management and stop-loss discipline; suitable only for experienced traders

strategies.name: Put Backspread (Long Convexity / Tail-Risk Buyer)
strategies.who_uses: Tail-risk hedge funds (e.g., Universa-style strategies), CTAs, macro funds buying crash convexity
strategies.view: bearish or tail-risk hedge; profits most on large downside moves
strategies.legs: Sell 1 ATM put + buy 2 (or more) OTM puts at a lower strike, same expiry. Usually structured for near-zero net premium so there is no net cost in calm markets.
strategies.edge_source: Provides asymmetric profit on large downside moves at minimal net cost. The premium from the sold ATM put finances the two long lower-strike puts. Convexity profile: small loss in moderate declines, large profit in crashes. Tail-risk funds use this to add convexity to equity portfolios at low ongoing cost.
strategies.main_risk: Loss zone between the sold ATM put and the two long puts: if the market drops moderately (e.g., 3–5%) but not severely (>8%), the position loses on the net.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — complex Greek profile with a loss zone; requires accurate understanding of the full payoff at all price levels; mispriced sizing can create large losses

strategies.name: Box Spread (Synthetic Loan / Risk-Free Arbitrage)
strategies.who_uses: Institutional arbitrageurs, prop desks, index funds exploiting temporary option mispricing
strategies.legs: Long call spread (buy lower-strike call, sell higher-strike call) + short put spread (sell lower-strike put, buy higher-strike put), same strikes and expiry. Net position replicates a risk-free zero-coupon bond.
strategies.edge_source: A correctly priced box costs exactly the present value of the difference between strikes. When mispriced, it constitutes a pure arbitrage (riskless locked-in profit). NSE index options are European-style, eliminating assignment risk and making box spreads cleaner than on US equity options.
strategies.main_risk: Execution and bid-ask risk when legging into four contracts simultaneously; regulatory or margin-rule changes mid-trade. Very thin net P&L makes it viable only for very large notional positions with extremely tight bid-ask spreads.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires four simultaneous legs with near-zero slippage; net P&L after transaction costs is negligible for retail-sized positions

strategies.name: Short ATM Weekly Straddle (Systematic Vol Selling)
strategies.who_uses: Indian proprietary options sellers, HNI traders, systematic vol-selling algorithms; was the dominant retail strategy pre-2024 SEBI reform
strategies.legs: Sell ATM call + sell ATM put at the same strike, same weekly expiry (now Tuesdays on NSE). Maximum profit if spot expires at or near the strike. Closed before expiry at 50% profit target (common systematic rule) or held to expiry.
strategies.edge_source: ATM straddle premium on NSE Nifty frequently exceeds the actual weekly index move (positive variance risk premium). Selling ATM straddles at weekly expiry monetizes this overpricing. This strategy (combined with holding to expiry) was the dominant pattern among individual traders identified in SEBI’s FY22–FY24 study, where the institutional counterparties were net sellers of options to retail buyers overall.
strategies.main_risk: Large moves beyond the combined premium received result in loss; theoretically unlimited loss on one side without hedging wings. SEBI’s 2024 ELM margin makes this more capital-intensive.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — requires close monitoring; a single large gap can wipe out months of collected premium; SEBI data show 93% of retail F&O traders lose over a multi-year horizon

strategies.name: Jade Lizard (Short Put + Short OTM Call Spread)
strategies.who_uses: Retail and professional traders who want to sell puts but eliminate upside risk
strategies.legs: Sell OTM put + sell OTM call + buy further OTM call (same expiry). Structure the total credit received to equal or exceed the width of the call spread so there is zero risk to the upside above the long call strike.
strategies.edge_source: Designed so total premium collected covers the entire call-spread width, eliminating all upside risk while generating net positive income. Collects premium from both put and call sides while capping the only risky direction (downside below the short put).
strategies.main_risk: Standard put risk on the downside: if the index falls sharply below the short put strike, losses can be very large. No upside risk if structured correctly.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — well-defined upside risk profile; suitable for traders comfortable with selling puts who want call-side risk removed

strategies.name: Synthetic Long Index (Options-Based Futures Replication)
strategies.who_uses: Institutional traders, arbitrageurs, prop desks managing delta exposure without additional futures exposure
strategies.legs: Buy ATM call + sell ATM put at the same strike and expiry. Creates a payoff profile equivalent to being long index futures from that strike. Can be done at any strike.
strategies.edge_source: Replicates index futures exposure using options. When futures trade at a premium or discount to theoretical fair value (cost of carry), an options-based synthetic can be cheaper or more capital-efficient than the actual future. Also used to create incremental delta exposure within position limits.
strategies.main_risk: Full downside exposure like owning the index; large notional exposure per lot post SEBI’s lot-size increase to ₹15L minimum (Nifty lot of 75 units). NSE index options are European-style so no early assignment risk.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — equivalent risk to holding the index leveraged; requires understanding of put-call parity and large capital backing

strategies.name: India VIX Futures Hedge / Long Volatility
strategies.who_uses: Sophisticated portfolio managers, systematic macro funds, tail-hedging desks; available on NSE since 2014
strategies.view: volatility — long during fear spikes and market sell-offs
strategies.legs: Long India VIX futures contracts; sized proportionally to the equity portfolio’s vega or as a fixed notional tail hedge. India VIX is NSE’s 30-day implied vol measure on Nifty options.
strategies.edge_source: India VIX spikes sharply and negatively correlates with Nifty returns during market sell-offs, providing natural hedge that pays off when equity portfolios decline most. Multiple studies confirm India VIX is a significant predictor of subsequent realized market volatility (Nuvama Research; ScienceDirect). Provides pure volatility exposure without delta baggage.
strategies.main_risk: Significant negative carry (roll cost) in the typical contango structure of VIX futures; sustained holding in calm markets generates losses. Settlement is cash-based against the VIX index level.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — VIX futures lot size and settlement complexity make it difficult for retail; no India VIX ETF equivalent available as in the US; primarily institutional

strategies.name: Trend/Momentum Strategy with Long OTM Option Tail Hedge
strategies.who_uses: Systematic trend-following funds (CTAs), macro hedge funds, multi-strategy managers blending trend with convexity
strategies.legs: Long Nifty futures (when uptrend signal active) or short futures (downtrend) + long OTM put (uptrend) or OTM call (downtrend) sized so premium is approximately 1–2% of portfolio per month. Alternatively: buy OTM calls/puts directly in the trend direction.
strategies.edge_source: Trend-following has well-documented long-run equity premium with strong performance in crisis periods. Long OTM options add positive convexity: large trend moves produce outsized profits while the downside from false signals is limited to the premium paid. Academic research shows trend + long options has superior Sharpe and lower drawdown than trend-only strategies.
strategies.main_risk: Ongoing cost of option premium in low-vol, range-bound markets; whipsaw in sideways regimes generates losses on both the futures position and the premium paid for options.
strategies.retail_suitability: medium — conceptually straightforward (buy trend + buy insurance), but correct sizing of both legs and option selection require quantitative skill

strategies.name: Risk Reversal (Directional Options Structure)
strategies.who_uses: Hedge funds with directional views, macro traders, FX-trained desks applying the structure to equity index options
strategies.view: bullish (sell put, buy call) or bearish (sell call, buy put)
strategies.legs: Sell OTM put + buy OTM call at approximately the same delta (e.g., both 25-delta), same expiry, for a near-zero net premium. Creates leveraged directional exposure with defined cost.
strategies.edge_source: Gives directional exposure at near-zero net cost by selling put protection to finance call buying (or vice versa). In markets with elevated put skew (common in equity indices), selling the expensive downside put and buying the relatively cheap upside call is a structurally favourable risk-reward for bullish views.
strategies.main_risk: If the market moves against the short option (e.g., index falls below the short put strike), losses can be large. Near-zero premium means the position behaves like a leveraged directional bet with no premium buffer.
strategies.retail_suitability: low — leveraged directional risk with limited premium income as a buffer; requires precise understanding of breakevens and max-loss scenarios

evidence.title: Dynamics of Variance Risk Premium in Indian Equity Index Options (Nifty 50)
evidence.finding: Using model-based and model-free techniques on Nifty options data, market-neutral straddles earned statistically significant negative returns (i.e., selling straddles was profitable), confirming that variance risk is priced in Indian equity index options. Realized variance consistently fell below implied variance, producing a positive and economically significant VRP. Transaction costs reduced but did not eliminate the profitability of short-volatility strategies on Nifty.
evidence.source_name: Dynamics of Variance Risk Premium: Evidence from India (2020) — Review of Economic Analysis / ScienceDirect

evidence.title: Nifty 50 VRP Structural Anatomy: 43 Million Option Bars (Aug 2022–Mar 2026)
evidence.finding: Using 43 million+ one-minute option bars, this SSRN study found VRP is positive on 74.9% of Nifty trading days with mean +1.208 vol points, AR(1) of 0.786, and 25.1% inversion rate. Transaction costs reduce gross profitable days to 72.4%, leaving a median net edge of +1.131 vol points. Critically, a structural epoch inversion emerged in early 2026 (mean VRP −4.63 vol points, statistically robust under Newey-West HAC corrections) driven by macro regime shift, demonstrating VRP is not unconditionally stable across all regimes.
evidence.source_name: Agarwal (2026) — The Variance Risk Premium in Nifty 50: A Structural Anatomy Across Nine Empirical Filters (SSRN)

evidence.title: Nifty VRP Drives Excess Returns in Volatility-Selling Strategies
evidence.finding: A study using India VIX as the implied variance proxy and log-return realized variance found that implied variance regularly exceeded realized variance in Indian equity options, producing a statistically significant positive VRP. The premium can be collected via India VIX futures shorts, synthetic short-variance swap positions, or delta-hedged short ATM straddles. Profitability persisted across multiple sub-periods but diminished in bear or high-volatility regimes.
evidence.source_name: Economic Sciences (2024) — Does the VRP from Nifty Options Drive Excess Returns in a Volatility-Selling Strategy?

evidence.title: CBOE S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT): 32-Year Risk-Adjusted Outperformance
evidence.finding: Over July 1986–December 2015, the CBOE PUT index posted gross compound returns of 10.1% with annualized standard deviation of 10.1% vs S&P 500’s 9.8% return and 15.3% vol. The PUT index’s Sharpe ratio (0.67) was 46% higher than the S&P 500’s (0.47). As of July 31 2025, the PUT 10-year annualized return was 7.2%. Performance figures are gross of transaction costs, which are materially higher for options than equities.
evidence.source_name: Bondarenko (2019) — Historical Performance of Put-Writing Strategies, CBOE Research

evidence.title: CBOE BXM Covered-Call Index: 40-Year Return vs S&P 500 (1986–2026)
evidence.finding: The CBOE BuyWrite Index (BXM), systematically selling near-month ATM covered calls against an S&P 500 position, delivered 8.5% annualized returns over 40 years (June 1986–June 2026) vs 11.1% for the S&P 500. However, BXM had substantially lower volatility; the Wilshire/CBOE 2019 study found all option-writing strategies had superior Sharpe ratios vs the S&P 500. Covered calls were most beneficial when the market returned 0–10% annually; they lagged significantly in strong bull markets.
evidence.source_name: Wilshire/CBOE Options-Based Benchmark Indexes Study (2019); 40-year BXM data via Thetix Blog (2026)

evidence.title: SEBI FY22–FY24: 93% of Indian F&O Traders Lose; FPIs and Props Capture Profits via Algos
evidence.finding: SEBI’s 2024 study of 1 crore+ individual traders found 93% lost money between FY22 and FY24, with aggregate individual losses exceeding ₹1.8 lakh crore. FPIs earned ₹28,000 crore and proprietary traders ₹33,000 crore in gross profits in FY24 alone. Of FPI profits, 97% came from algorithmic entities; of prop-trader profits, 96% came from algo entities. Only 13% of retail traders used any algorithm (and that figure is overstated).
evidence.source_name: SEBI (2024) — Updated Study: Analysis of Profits and Losses in Equity F&O Segment FY22–FY24

evidence.title: Nifty Options Overnight vs Intraday VRP: Separable Predictability Horizons
evidence.finding: Research in Journal of Futures Markets (2025) found that Nifty options display negative overnight returns and positive intraday returns. The intraday VRP component performs better at shorter prediction horizons while overnight VRP performs better at longer horizons, suggesting that nontrading period effects (US and Asian market news, overnight risk-aversion buildup) are a distinct and important contributor to India’s index option risk premium separate from the intraday component.
evidence.source_name: Papagelis (2025) — The Variance Risk Premium Over Trading and Nontrading Periods, Journal of Futures Markets (Wiley)

evidence.title: SEBI FY25 Update: Individual Trader Losses Rose 41% to ₹1.06 Lakh Crore; Participation Declining
evidence.finding: SEBI’s July 2025 study showed individual losses rose 41% to ₹1,05,603 crore in FY25 vs ₹74,812 crore in FY24. Over 91% of traders made losses (unchanged from prior years), with median individual loss of ₹1.1 lakh. The number of unique traders fell from 61.4 lakh in Q1 FY25 to 42.7 lakh in Q4 FY25, suggesting SEBI’s October 2024 reforms (lot-size increase and weekly expiry restriction) began reducing retail over-participation, with Q4 FY25 showing the first sequential reduction in aggregate losses.
evidence.source_name: Business Standard / SEBI Equity Derivatives Trader Loss Study: FY25 Update (July 2025)

github.what: Python library for option prices, implied volatility, and Greeks (Black, Black-Scholes, Black-Scholes-Merton). Core uses Peter Jäckel’s LetsBeRational for extremely fast and accurate IV solving. Supports analytical and numerical Greeks.

Vectorized extension of py_vollib supporting NumPy arrays and pandas Series/DataFrames. Prices thousands of option contracts and calculates Greeks efficiently in batch mode; dramatically faster than looping py_vollib calls.

Options pricing open-source library implementing Black-Scholes (equity options), Garman-Kohlhagen (FX options), and Merton (dividend-adjusted) models. Returns callPrice, putPrice, delta, theta, rho, vega, gamma, and impliedVolatility for all models.

Lightweight Python library for evaluating multi-leg options strategies: computes P/L profile on a user-defined target date, range of profitable prices, Greeks (delta, theta, rho, vega, gamma), resulting debit or credit, and maximum/minimum returns.

opstrat 2.0: Python library for visualizing options strategies with interactive Plotly figures. Hover for per-leg and combined P/L; max profit, max loss, and breakevens solved analytically and shown on every chart. Dark/light theme, HTML export.
Original opstrat package (v0.1.7 on PyPI): matplotlib-based option strategy payoff visualization. Available via pip. The hedge-design fork (opstrat 2.0) is the modern Plotly-based successor.

Python library to download live and historical stock, index, and F&O (futures and options) data from NSE and RBI. Supports new NSE website, powerful CLI, built-in caching to avoid rate-limits, and optional pandas support. Covers NSE stocks F&O, index F&O with strike and expiry filtering.

NSE data library with comprehensive coverage: capital market data, bhav copies, derivatives price-volume data, participant-wise OI and volume, live option chains (nse_live_option_chain()), FII derivatives statistics, and F&O ban-period securities. Suitable for building institutional flow dashboards.

Unofficial Python API for NSE India with dedicated session management (httpx.Client with connection pooling, browser-like headers, automatic cookie persistence). Returns compiled option chains with max pain, PCR, ATM strikes; handles throttling (3 req/sec default) and exponential-backoff retries automatically.

Production-ready pipeline for downloading, enriching, and analysing 5 years of NSE F&O bhavcopy data. Fuses Bhavcopy files, Yahoo spot prices, FBIL MIFOR interest-rate curves, and earnings calendars; computes IV, RV, Greeks, IV-percentile/rank; stores to PostgreSQL or JSON. Suitable for systematic strategy research.

Backtesting and live-trading framework specifically for NSE Nifty 50 index options-selling strategies. Uses NSE EOD data; targets short-strangle and related short-vol strategies; includes position sizing and P&L tracking.

Backtests Nifty 50 index options strategies on real NSE end-of-day data and displays results in an interactive web dashboard. Built-in support for common Nifty strategies; Python-based with Streamlit-style output.

Nimble Python backtesting and statistics library for options strategies. Supports 38 built-in strategies from simple calls/puts to iron condors, butterflies, condors, ratio spreads, collars, and calendars. Designed for rapid strategy research: go from a hypothesis about iron-condor DTE and profit targets to detailed performance statistics without spreadsheets.

Lightweight, fast Python backtesting framework for trading strategies using OHLC candlestick data. Widely used as the general-purpose backtesting layer under NSE options research projects. Interactive HTML charts with Bokeh. Note: dormant since August 2024 per upstream tracking.

Comprehensive Python platform for NSE options traders: analyzes, calculates, and visualizes multi-leg options strategies with real-time P&L tracking across multiple Indian brokers (ICICI Direct, Nuvama). Strategy calculator supporting straddle, strangle, iron condor, and custom legs.

Options portfolio backtester with realistic execution, Greeks-aware risk management, and contract-level inventory. Includes tools for strategy sweeps, tail-risk hedge analysis, and signal-based timing research across historical option data.

Real-time NSE option chain retrieval and analysis for indices and 141+ stocks. Continuously refreshes the option chain and displays trends in OI, change in OI, PCR, max-pain, and other technical indicators. Supports multiple simultaneous instances with different symbols. Python 3.6+.

Python code companion to the book ‘Option Greeks Strategies & Backtesting in Python’. Covers Greeks calculation, strategy construction, and EOD backtesting of named strategies using Indian market data. Educational reference for systematic Nifty options strategy research.

caveats: EOD data cannot capture the intraday dynamics on which the most profitable documented strategies depend. Expiry-day theta selling, gamma scalping, delta-hedged market making, and 0-DTE short options all require intraday (tick or minute-bar) data; backtests using daily close prices will misstate P&L, entry/exit timing, and drawdowns for these strategies.

Transaction costs are substantial and strategy-specific: bid-ask spreads for OTM Nifty options can be 10–30% of the option premium, SPAN margins are dynamic, and SEBI’s 2024 Extreme Loss Margin adds 2% on expiry-day short positions. Many studies that show a positive VRP report gross P&L; net returns after realistic costs are materially lower and can turn a theoretical edge negative.

Retail traders lose money at a very high rate: SEBI’s official studies show 91–93% of individual F&O traders incurred losses over multi-year periods (FY22–FY25). Any backtest that shows a positive return for a retail-oriented options-selling strategy must be evaluated critically, as selection bias, look-ahead, and the absence of real-world execution costs likely explain much of the apparent edge.

Regime changes and structural breaks invalidate historical backtests: SEBI’s October 2024 reforms (lot-size tripling to 75 units, weekly expiry reduction, ELM), the September 2025 expiry-day shift from Thursday to Tuesday, and the Jane Street enforcement action all represent structural breaks. Strategy results from FY22–FY24 data may not generalize to the current market structure.

Capital and lot-size requirements are a binding constraint for retail: the minimum Nifty index option notional is ₹15 lakh per lot post-November 2024. Multi-leg strategies (iron condor, butterfly, calendar spread) multiply margin requirements, making systematic options selling strategies practically inaccessible to small retail participants even if the theoretical edge is documented.

Survivorship and reporting bias affect strategy catalogues: strategies discussed in public research are those that worked in the observed historical period. Strategies that failed catastrophically (short gamma desks blown up by large moves, retail traders who stopped trading after losing) are underrepresented in published literature, overstating the apparent success rate of documented approaches.
unverified: The original nsepython PyPI package (by Prashant Pandey / zerodha-unofficial) was widely cited in 2021–2022 but its current maintenance status and NSE API compatibility as of 2026 could not be confirmed; NseIndiaApi and nselib are verified active alternatives.

Media reports (Business World, July 2025) indicate SEBI was also investigating Millennium Management’s India activities after the Jane Street order; however, no confirmed SEBI circular or interim order against Millennium was verified as of this research date.

Garg & Vipul (2015) is cited in multiple secondary sources as finding short-volatility strategies on Nifty to be significantly profitable; the original journal citation could not be directly read during this session and exact effect-size numbers from that paper are from secondary sources only.
